title: A Free Music Festival Will Warm Up College Football's Big Game
summary:
College football's biggest game is getting a musical warm-up, and it will not cost fans a cent. The free AT&T Playoff Playlist Live festival will take place on January 23-24 in Las Vegas, just before the 2027 College Football Playoff National Championship on January 25.

The championship game will see two top teams compete at Allegiant Stadium. First, a heavy-hitting lineup of DJs will provide the pump-up music at the festival, held at Las Vegas' Grand Prix Plaza, just off the Strip. The two-day festival is called AT&T Playoff Playlist Live, the CFP Music Festival. Doors open at 3 p.m. on both days.

Night one brings David Guetta, Marshmello, Alison Wonderland, Honeyluv, and Girl Math, the duo made up of Nala and VNSSA. Day two features John Summit, Fisher, Sofi Tukker, Korolova, and DJ Skilah. All of them are DJs and electronic music stars.

"No city embraces the variety of music genres like Las Vegas," said Ryan Allen Hall, the College Football Playoff's senior director of public events and sponsorships. "But it's clear, electronic music is the pulse." Las Vegas, he said, "simply does EDM like only a select few in the entire world."

The best part, Hall said, is the price. "The magic for us is to bring together this stacked lineup in Las Vegas and to charge the fans absolutely nothing," he said. The free concerts are part of the championship's promise to give fans a world-class experience during National Championship week.

Last year's festival took place in Miami Beach, with John Summit, Calvin Harris, Peso Pluma, and Latin Mafia performing for a crowd of about 50,000. It was the largest concert ever seen on South Beach, Hall said. This year, the organizers say they are here to do the same for Las Vegas.
why_it_matters: Big games are about more than the game itself: they bring music, fans, and whole cities together. A free festival means everyone can join the fun, not just people with tickets.
